hands.unsupported: dsh 0.1.0-rc.6 replaces its tool surface only through a profile plugin (presentAs/restrict/guard/register on the scoped tools service); no CLI flag disables its shell and file tools or adds an MCP server, so the one boxed tool cannot be expressed without a plugin. Re-measured on 0.1.2-rc.1 (2026-09-04): the launcher and headless flags are unchanged; the tools plugin reads a DSH_TOOLS_MODE environment value whose vocabulary the release does not document, so it is not relied on. The plugin is the next slice.

headless-work.reason: the headless runner mints its own agent: lib/index.js calls agents.create with session-${randomUUID()} and applies its followup to that agent, and its whole config schema is {task}
limitations: the launcher's --resume <session> appears only in a TUI-profile example and reaches the app verbatim; headless startup parses one positional, the task, and --help
dsh-agent-loop admits Config.agents[].resumeSessionId and dsh-agent exposes agents.resume, but they restore a CONFIGURED agent and the headless caller does not run its admitted task on that agent

closing that gap needs a mechanism this change is not authorized to use: replacing the installed runner plugin, monkey-patching agents.create, overriding UUID generation, editing the installed package or substituting the TUI
the retained per-invocation transcript directory is a locator, not a provider handle; no measured equivalence exists
the separate hands/tools plugin deferral above is a different matter and is not what blocks this shape
